ranking.rationale: Strongest candidate: directly measured +0.00221 primary lift, full coverage, positive lift on all four holdout dates, narrow ablation, and low runtime and leakage risk.
Builds on the only positive feature direction and tests bounded nonlinear context personalization with moderate runtime risk and low leakage risk, though it duplicates some of c01 and expands scope.
Uses the fully covered, consistently positive request-context signal with low runtime and leakage risk; less scope than c12, but the nonlinear representation is not directly measured.
Very safe and interpretable single-field ablation directly tied to the positive screen, but expected gain is limited because tab is only part of the measured group.
Narrow, cheap, and leakage-safe temporal test, but the cyclic encoding is speculative and expected lift is smaller than the broader context ablation.
Potentially aligns training with within-user evaluation, but evidence is indirect and the stated medium leakage and runtime risks reduce its value.
A contained architecture test with moderate runtime risk, but it lacks direct architecture evidence, omits the measured request-context signal, and may overfit identity interactions.
Cheap, clean, and interpretable, but weekday alone has weak expected lift and no field-level evidence supporting it.
Potential interaction benefit is plausible, but it stacks a cross branch onto an embedding-plus-MLP concept, creating duplication and excessive architectural scope without direct evidence.
The top-rank objective is interesting, but ListNet depends on valid mixed-label groups, has high runtime risk and medium leakage risk, and lacks direct measured loss evidence.
Pairwise loss is aligned with GAUC, but sampled-pair construction, group coverage, high runtime, and medium leakage risk make it a poor scarce-experiment choice.

Combines request-context features with a loss change relative to the seed, increasing scope and confounding attribution; it also carries high runtime and medium leakage risk with weak direct evidence.
